title: How the Market Prices Options Through Distributions
text: When we place a trade, the market has a few things priced out. The location is where the middle generally sits, and that's like the directional claim that you might make. Width is how far that distribution actually spreads, and this is way more of a volatility claim as compared to other functions. Then there's the shape. The shape is the symmetry or asymmetry, and if you look at this specific curve that I have plotted here, it's fatter on the left side, and that's often known as put skew. And then there's term, which is that dashed line, and all that's saying is that a different expiration has a different distribution.
